$comment: FEAT-030 (engine.core AC-1 interim-ruling debt closure): master doc §3's real-time pacing knob -- '1 game month ~= 8 real minutes (config: secondsPerMonthAt1x, default 480)'. Previously a single named Go var (internal/engine/core/clock.go's DefaultSecondsPerMonthAt1x) with no data-file backing because foundation.data's original eight section-24 config files had nowhere for a pacing value to live (MOD-012's interim ruling, 2026-08-09). This is that ninth file, added the same way market.json was (MOD-020 ruling 1) rather than growing the original eight-file set's own doc comment. Placeholder per the balance-number regime: secondsPerMonthAt1x's original VALUE (480) was an unchanged directional placeholder carried over verbatim from the Go var it replaced -- this file's job is sourcing (data-driven, not hardcoded), never re-picking the number. Aaron ruling, 2026-08-21 (watch-it-live milestone): at 480, a game month took 8 real minutes and one daily tick landed only every 16 real seconds, so 'watch the city live' meant watching something nearly static -- not useful for demoing the loop. Aaron approved 30 explicitly as a second placeholder, under the same balance-number regime as the first: a watchability placeholder, not a designed pace. It makes one tick roughly one real second and a game month roughly 30 real seconds -- fast enough to be watchable. Neither 480 nor 30 is a tuned balance value; the real pacing constant is still a later, Aaron-reviewed tuning pass (per docs/planning/acceptance/balance.harness.md), to be proposed once there is enough simulation depth for pacing to mean something.
